channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Attackers chained Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to take root on fully patched VPNs; one link still has no patch
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that attackers had chained three Connect Secure flaws to gain root on fully patched appliances at a limited number of customers. Two of the flaws are fixed under a single identifier, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), which CISA added to KEV that day with a 16 October deadline. The third, a privilege escalation, has no CVE and no patch; Ivanti says a fix will follow in the coming weeks. Volexity, which found the chain during incident response, tracks the actor as UTA0576, a new actor; exploitation dates to at least early October. The intruders left no web shell: they stole domain credentials, pulled LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, and wiped logs. Volexity and CISA warn that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may miss this compromise. No utility victim has been named, but these VPNs often carry staff and vendor access toward control-system networks (editorial assessment). - Ivanti security advisory for CVE-2026-104935 and CISA KEV listing, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); Volexity analysis, 13 Oct 2026; reported by SecurityWeek, CyberScoop and Cybersecurity Dive - Disclosed and KEV-listed 13 Oct 2026; exploited since at least early October

item.title: [Critical] A fourth critical Citrix NetScaler flaw means some appliances patched for the exploited zero-days must be upgraded again
item.category: Incident — Exploited remote-access appliance zero-days, CISA KEV; fourth critical flaw patched
item.description: Citrix published bulletin CTX697191 on 8 October for CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5), a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider that Citrix says may lead to code execution or denial of service. The builds that fixed the September zero-days stay exposed when the appliance acts as a SAML identity provider, so those customers must upgrade again; there is no workaround. Citrix says it is not aware of exploitation of the new flaw, and it is not in KEV. It lands in the middle of an active campaign: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (both CVSS v4 9.5) were exploited before patches existed and entered KEV on 27 September, and CVE-2026-88779, a denial-of-service flaw according to Citrix and watchTowr, followed on 4 October. CISA has warned that attackers use it to force reboots so that code planted through CVE-2026-88771 runs, and has published Sigma detection rules. Mandiant counts dozens of victim organizations and calls the actors suspected state-nexus without naming a group; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78 targeted organizations, and Shadowserver sees more than 20,000 exposed or potentially vulnerable appliances. Intruders planted web shells, and Mandiant warns that upgrading alone does not remove access already gained. No power-sector victim has been named, but NetScaler often fronts contractor and field-staff access at utilities, so an unhunted appliance is a possible first hop toward EMS, SCADA and substation networks (editorial assessment). - Citrix bulletins CTX697191 (8 Oct 2026), CTX697174 and CTX697096; CISA KEV listings 27 Sep and 4 Oct 2026 (primary); Mandiant, Arctic Wolf, watchTowr and Shadowserver findings reported by SecurityWeek, Cybersecurity Dive and The Hacker News - First two flaws KEV-listed 27 Sep 2026; third 4 Oct 2026; fourth flaw disclosed 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication bypass CVE-2026-76504 was exploited as a zero-day; there is no workaround
item.category: Incident — Exploited SD-WAN management zero-day, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) on 30 September: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager mishandles URI encoding, so a crafted HTTP request can bypass an API authentication rule and give a remote, unauthenticated attacker administrative access. Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in September, and CISA added the flaw to KEV the same day with a 3 October federal deadline, now passed. Cisco revised the advisory on 2 October. There is no workaround; a temporary Live Protect shield gives partial protection but may block some legitimate users. BleepingComputer counts this as the fifth exploited SD-WAN zero-day of 2026. No actor, victim or sector has been named. SD-WAN Manager pushes policy to the overlay that many utilities use to link offices, plants and substations, so administrative access to it is a position from which traffic paths toward field sites could be changed (editorial assessment). - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU, 30 Sep 2026, revised 2 Oct (primary); CISA KEV 30 Sep 2026; reported by BleepingComputer - Disclosed and KEV-listed 30 Sep 2026; advisory v1.1 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Three clusters, including an APT and a ransomware operator, are exploiting Cisco firewall-manager flaws CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316
item.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco and CISA confirmed on 9 September that CVE-2026-20079, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass that lets an unauthenticated attacker run scripts and gain root on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center, is being exploited; CISA added it to KEV with a 12 September deadline, now passed. Cisco Talos describes three clusters. UAT-12197 used it to plant a web shell and pull authentication data from internal databases. UAT-11823, which Talos assesses with high confidence to be an APT, got in through CVE-2026-20079 or static credentials, exploiting CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3, low-privilege remote login) as well, then used a reverse shell, configuration-harvesting scripts and a variant of the Cyclops Blink modular implant. UAT-11988, which Talos assesses to be a ransomware operator, entered through CVE-2026-20316, used FMC’s built-in tools for reconnaissance and credential harvesting, and later deployed ransomware on selected endpoints. Cisco released hotfixes for both flaws, and Talos said a broader hardening release would follow in mid-September. Talos’s post, last modified 21 September, names no victims or sectors. FMC configures the firewalls that separate corporate networks from generation, substation and DER control. - Cisco Talos analysis, published 9 Sep and updated 21 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV listing 9 Sep 2026 - Exploitation confirmed 9 Sep 2026; Talos update 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed credential theft against FortiGate VPNs is still active, and energy is among the targeted sectors
item.category: Incident — Active credential-theft campaign against firewall and VPN gateways; no CVE
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October that the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways is still active. There is no CVE: the agencies say attackers exploit reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, and researchers describe credential stuffing and spraying, offline hash cracking and a sniffer that captures authentication traffic. Intruders create their own administrator accounts and sometimes delete or reset the real ones, locking owners out, and the access is resold; the FBI advisory links it to Payload ransomware, and SOCRadar says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments from it. SOCRadar’s figure of 86,644 working device credentials across 194 countries dates from 19 June; it is not a new count. The agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, including energy. No compromise of an OT system has been described, but FortiGates commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and in front of remote access to plants and substations (editorial assessment). - FBI and US Secret Service joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, 6 Oct 2026 (primary); reported by Cybersecurity Dive and The Hacker News - Warning issued 6 Oct 2026; credential count dates from 19 Jun 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet FortiMail flaw CVE-2026-104286 was exploited before a fix existed; Fortinet’s 5 October update now lists fixed releases
item.category: Incident — Exploited email-security gateway zero-day, CISA KEV
item.description: Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-26-175 on 1 October for CVE-2026-104286 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw in FortiMail that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on the appliance with crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests. Fortinet says the flaw has been reported exploited in the wild, and CISA added it to KEV on 1 October with a 4 October deadline. No fixed build was available at disclosure; Fortinet’s 5 October update lists 8.0.2, 7.6.7 and 7.4.9, and tells 7.2 users to move to the 7.4 branch or later. Fortinet still urges its workarounds: turn off the IBE feature, restrict the webmail interface to trusted networks, and block POST requests to /ibe paths that contain “../”. No actor or victims have been disclosed. FortiMail sits on the corporate side rather than in control networks, but a compromised mail gateway is a trusted platform for phishing operations and engineering staff (editorial assessment). - Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-175, 1 Oct 2026, updated 5 Oct (primary); CISA KEV 1 Oct 2026; reported by SecurityWeek - Disclosed and KEV-listed 1 Oct 2026; fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] CenterPoint Energy’s breach reached more than 1 million Texans, its state filing shows; the company reports no operational impact
item.category: Incident — Confirmed customer-data breach at a US electric & gas utility; scope update
item.description: CenterPoint Energy has told the Texas Attorney General’s Office that 1,062,060 Texas residents were affected by the breach it disclosed in September, with names, addresses, Social Security numbers and driver’s license numbers exposed, SecurityWeek reported on 15 October. Residents of Indiana, Minnesota and Ohio may also be affected, and the overall total is not yet clear. CenterPoint says the incident did not affect its operations. In its 15 September SEC filing the company said an unauthorized third party obtained customer personal information through an externally facing system, and that it learned of the breach from the actor’s own public post: a 2.5 GB archive offered on 12 September with a claim of about 7.5 million records and a threat to attack “the main infrastructure” next. The entry point and the actor remain undisclosed, and the 7.5 million figure is unconfirmed. This is an IT-side data breach, not an OT compromise, but stolen identity data is raw material for phishing and social engineering against utility staff and customers. - CenterPoint Energy filing with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, reported by SecurityWeek; CenterPoint SEC filing, 15 Sep 2026 (primary) - Data posted for sale 12 Sep 2026; SEC disclosure 15 Sep 2026; Texas figure reported 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] A suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor exploited a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day from late August, Google says
item.category: Incident — Exploited remote-support zero-day, suspected state espionage
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group said on 15 October that a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support, CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4.0 9.3), was exploited from late August, and attributes the activity to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, based on overlapping tools and techniques. The attackers gained root on Remote Support appliances, harvested credentials, deleted logs and used the product’s file-transfer feature to pull documents from users’ desktops, deploying the SAWFLY web shell and the BARECLAW tunneler. Versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. BeyondTrust identified the defect in late September, shipped patch BT26-05-RS on 8 October and had patched its SaaS customers by 9 October; self-hosted appliances without automatic updates must be patched by hand, and releases older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first. The flaw was not in KEV as of CISA’s 15 October catalog, and GTIG names no victims or sectors. Remote-support tools like this are how many OEMs, integrators and help desks reach plant workstations, so the relevance to power operators is the vendor-access path (editorial assessment). - Google Threat Intelligence Group analysis and BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05, 15 Oct 2026 (primary); reported by SecurityWeek - Exploited from late August 2026; fix released 8 Oct 2026; disclosed 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] FBI seizes domains behind China-linked scanning and phishing tools whose targets included a US power company
item.category: Threat Intelligence — US seizure of China-linked scanning and phishing infrastructure; a US power company among named targets
item.description: On 8 October the Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorized seizures of domains used to run Microscan, a Python web application with more than 1,300 penetration-testing scripts, and FishHub, a spear-phishing and malware-delivery platform. US authorities say both were built and run by China-based Integrity Technology Group, the company sanctioned last year and tied to a 2024 botnet takedown; CyberScoop calls the tools Flax Typhoon-linked, while Cybersecurity Dive says the activity mimics the group tracked as Flax Typhoon. A Mirai-variant IoT botnet supported Microscan. Court documents list Microscan targets including a South Carolina power company, gas and power companies in Taiwan, airports in Japan and Poland and a multinational NGO; FishHub was used against Taiwanese universities. No compromise of the power company or the Taiwanese utilities has been confirmed. A joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory accompanies the action, and CISA’s Chris Butera said China-affiliated actors keep positioning themselves inside critical-infrastructure networks, OT systems included. - DOJ/FBI domain seizures and joint FBI/CISA/NSA advisory, 8 Oct 2026 (primary); reported by CyberScoop and Cybersecurity Dive - Announced 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and FBI: a compromised ICS integrator held utilities’ SCADA data — limit what yours can reach
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Joint CISA/FBI guidance drawn from a compromised ICS integrator
item.description: CISA and the FBI released a joint fact sheet on 24 September, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators.” Its motivating case: in March–April 2025, foreign actors inside a US industrial automation company that does system integration and SCADA programming for customers including power utilities and transportation entities searched for “customers” and “SCADA” and staged nine archives of about 800 files — customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics — for exfiltration. The agencies do not name the company, the actor or its country, and do not say any utility was breached. Their advice: write security and supply-chain requirements into integrator contracts, apply least privilege, route remote access through monitored, on-demand channels, know what data integrators hold and where, and be able to operate if an integrator is compromised. - CISA/FBI joint fact sheet (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber and SecurityWeek - Released 24 Sep 2026; cites a March–April 2025 intrusion at the integrator

item.title: [Low] Nozomi telemetry: energy, utilities and waste rose to third for OT alerts per organization this summer
item.category: Research — Vendor OT/IoT telemetry for June–August 2026
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs’ review of June–August 2026 telemetry from its customers ranks manufacturing first for alerts per organization and transportation second, with energy, utilities and waste moving up to third in place of government. Credential-related techniques made up roughly a third of detections. Among alerts it could tie to an actor, Nozomi attributes close to half to Scattered Spider, and Russia-linked or Russian-speaking actors together account for more than a third. Siemens PLCs and Rockwell products were among the most-detected vulnerable products, and Nozomi says 58% of this year’s vulnerabilities rate High or Critical, against 48% in 2025. These are alert counts from Nozomi’s own sensors, not confirmed intrusions, and the ranking reflects its customer base. - Nozomi Networks Labs blog, 12 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 12 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Critical unauthenticated code-execution flaw in GPA’s openPDC and openHistorian grid-data software; fixes are out
item.category: Advisory — Synchrophasor data concentrator and historian, unauthenticated remote code execution, no known exploitation
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-281-02, published 8 October, covers the Grid Protection Alliance’s open-source openPDC phasor data concentrator and openHistorian time-series historian. The most serious flaw, CVE-2026-100730 (CVSS v3.1 9.8, v4.0 9.3), is a deserialization bug in the service console: where Windows Authentication is not in use, an unauthenticated attacker on the network can reach it and run code as the service account. Other flaws in the advisory leave data publishers without authentication in default configurations, exposing topology information and STTP data exchange: CVE-2026-105281 (v3.1 7.5) and CVE-2026-85479 (v3.1 5.3). openPDC 2.9.482 and openHistorian 2.8.585 fix them; the Docker image is not fixed. New installs bind publishers to the loopback interface, but upgraded installs keep their old binding and must be checked by hand. CISA reports no known exploitation. These servers sit between substation phasor measurements and control-center analytics, so a compromised one is a foothold between networks (editorial assessment). - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-281-02 and CVE records issued by CISA as CNA (primary); CISA bulletin of six ICS advisories - Published 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Unauthenticated firmware upload in end-of-life Hitachi Energy RTU500 firmware; the fix is migration to a supported branch
item.category: Advisory — Substation RTU end-of-life firmware, unauthenticated firmware upload, no known exploitation
item.description: On 6 October CISA republished Hitachi Energy advisory 8DBD000251, first issued on 29 September, as ICSA-26-279-06. It covers six vulnerabilities in end-of-life RTU500 series CMU firmware, 11.x and earlier. The most serious, CVE-2026-8065 (CVSS v3.1 9.1), is missing authentication on the firmware-update endpoint, which lets an unauthenticated attacker upload arbitrary firmware with a crafted request; CVE-2026-8066 (9.1) is an unauthenticated directory traversal in file upload, and the list includes an old VxWorks debug-agent flaw, CVE-2010-2965 (9.8). Dragos reported the findings. Supported firmware is not affected, and Hitachi Energy’s remedy is to move to 12.7.8, 13.9.1 or later. CISA lists the Energy sector and reports no known exploitation. The same batch covered Hitachi Energy Asset Suite, where an unauthenticated test servlet allows configuration upload (CVE-2026-7395, 8.1; fix in 9.9.1 when available), and REB500 busbar protection, whose libexpat flaws are fixed in 8.3.4.0. RTU500s link substations and field sites to the control center, so attacker-supplied firmware on one would put code directly in the telecontrol path (editorial assessment). - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-279-06, republishing Hitachi Energy PSIRT advisory 8DBD000251 (primary); CISA ICSA-26-279-03 and -05 for Asset Suite and REB500 - Hitachi Energy advisory 29 Sep 2026; CISA republication 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] October ICS Patch Tuesday: fixes for Siemens CROSSBOW and Schneider Sage RTUs, but no fix yet for S7-1500 web-server flaws
item.category: Advisory — October ICS Patch Tuesday, grid-relevant items, no known exploitation
item.description: Siemens and Schneider Electric published their October advisories on 13 October; SecurityWeek counts 17 from Siemens. Three matter most to utilities. Siemens SSA-508506 fixes 11 flaws in RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW, Siemens’ access manager for remote engineering connections to substation devices (our description), including SQL injection and retrieval of administrator credentials, with a top CVSS v3.1 score of 8.8; V6.0 fixes them. Siemens SSA-591731 covers eight web-server flaws in S7-1500, ET 200SP and related CPUs (CVSS v3.1 9.6) that could let an attacker run code in an authorized user’s browser and act on the PLC with that user’s rights; all versions are affected and only mitigations exist. Schneider’s SEVD-2026-286-02 says Sage RTUs (1410, 1430, 1450, 2400, 3030 Magnum and 4400) do not adequately verify firmware authenticity, so modified firmware could be loaded when an administrator starts an update (CVE-2026-102250, v3.1 7.2); firmware C3414-500-S02L0 fixes it. Siemens also updated SSA-794185 on RADIUS (BlastRADIUS) in SIPROTEC and SICAM products, and CISA’s ICSA-26-286-01, which lists the Energy sector, covers an Inductive Automation Ignition privilege escalation (CVE-2026-92817, 8.8; fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9). None is reported exploited or in KEV. - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-508506, SSA-591731 and SSA-794185; Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-286-02; CISA ICSA-26-286-01 (primary); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup - Published 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] ABB’s PCM600 relay-engineering tool has two local flaws and no fixed version yet, only configuration workarounds
item.category: Advisory — Protection-relay engineering software, local privilege escalation, no fixed version
item.description: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-274-03 on 1 October for ABB’s Protection and Control IED Manager PCM600, versions 2.14 and earlier; ABB’s own advisories are dated 28 September. CVE-2026-15952 (CVSS v3.1 6.4, v4 7.1) is an incorrect permission assignment: PCM600’s Scheduler Service runs as LocalSystem while granting permissions to standard users, so an attacker with local access and valid credentials could escalate privileges. CVE-2026-15953 (v3.1 5.0, v4 5.6) is a path traversal in archive processing that could write files outside the intended directory; it needs local access and user interaction. CISA lists the Energy sector and reports no known public exploitation. ABB has released no fixed version, only mitigations. Neither flaw is remotely exploitable, but PCM600 is the tool engineers use to manage protection and control IEDs, so the workstations it runs on deserve the same care as the relays (editorial assessment). - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-274-03, 1 Oct 2026 (primary); ABB advisories 2NGA003170 and 2NGA003179, 28 Sep 2026 - ABB advisories 28 Sep 2026; CISA advisory 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] FERC staff CIP audit lessons: late-registered new generation, aggregated low-impact control and AI tools inside CIP networks
item.category: Regulation — FERC staff report on lessons learned from FY2026 CIP audits
item.description: On 13 October FERC’s Office of Electric Reliability published a staff report on lessons from its fiscal-2026 CIP audits. Most cybersecurity processes reviewed met the mandatory standards, but auditors found three recurring gaps. Some owners registered new generation late, or had not categorized BES Cyber Systems under CIP-002-5.1a, including inverter-based resources already synchronized and above the threshold; staff traces this to misreading the Commercial Operation Date, and one entity delayed registration for more than a year. In two scenarios, low-impact systems controlled by a non-registered parent over affiliated operators, or by one contractor serving several unaffiliated operators, met medium-impact criteria once their combined control was counted. And entities are bringing what the report calls super intelligence (SI) tools, such as chatbots, assistants and automated analytics, into CIP-networked environments; most had applied controls, but practices varied, and staff warns such tools can open unexpected lateral-movement or access paths. The report is non-binding; it suggests NERC consider more guidance or changes to standards or registration. - FERC news release and staff report Lessons Learned from Commission-Led CIP Reliability Audits (primary); reported by Industrial Cyber, 15 Oct - Released 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] CISA’s CIRCIA incident-reporting final rule is under White House review; reporting duties start only once it is published
item.category: Policy — Federal cyber incident-reporting rule under White House review
item.description: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged receipt of CISA’s final Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act rule (RIN 1670-AA04) on 1 October, starting the review that comes before publication. The rule text is not public, so its final scope and definitions are not yet known. The statute calls for reporting covered cyber incidents within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours, but those duties begin only on dates the final rule sets. The statutory deadline passed in October 2025 and CISA’s later targets slipped; HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before year-end. Power-sector participants in a GAO roundtable released 28 September already cited overlapping reporting rules, including NERC CIP, and every participant named the forthcoming CIRCIA rule as a concern. - OIRA EO 12866 review record for RIN 1670-AA04 (primary); reported by HIPAA Journal and Paubox; GAO-26-109197 reported by Cybersecurity Dive - Received for review 1 Oct 2026; no effective date yet

item.title: [Info] DOE launches a $100 million cybersecurity technical-assistance partnership for cooperative, municipal and small electric utilities
item.category: Policy — DOE cybersecurity technical assistance for small electric utilities
item.description: DOE’s Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) announced on 1 October the $100 million Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity (RMUC) Advanced Cybersecurity Technical Assistance partnership, administered by DOE’s partnership intermediary ConnectWerx. Applicant organizations must have formal partnerships with at least six qualifying electric utilities: cooperatives, municipal utilities or small investor-owned utilities. Funded work covers assessments and planning, workforce training and certification, exercises, tool implementation, verification and validation, and threat-information sharing. DOE’s announcement gives no application deadline and points applicants to ConnectWerx for details. It creates no new requirement, but for utilities without in-house OT security staff it is a route to outside assessment and exercise help. - DOE CESER announcement, 1 Oct 2026 (primary); reported by Industrial Cyber - Announced 1 Oct 2026; no application deadline stated
